item.title: Nadi woman's death classified as murder
item.description: The death of a woman in her 20s, whose body was found in Nadi on Thursday, has been classified as murder by Police. Police say her body was discovered near a complex in Nadi.
item.content:encoded:
The death of a woman in her 20s, whose body was found in Nadi on Thursday, has been classified as murder by Police.

Police say her body was discovered near a complex in Nadi.

Meanwhile, the death of a man whose body was found floating in the Labasa River on Friday is yet to be classified, as a post-mortem examination has not been conducted.

Police say investigations into both cases are continuing.

item.title: Police urge parents to monitor children following concerns along Khalsa Road
item.description: Police are urging parents to monitor their children's whereabouts following concerns raised about young people gathering along Khalsa Road in the evenings. A concerned resident has told fijivillage News that children, including girls wearing school uniforms, have been seen in the area after 8pm without adult supervision.
item.content:encoded:
Police are urging parents to monitor their children's whereabouts following concerns raised about young people gathering along Khalsa Road in the evenings.

A concerned resident has told fijivillage News that children, including girls wearing school uniforms, have been seen in the area after 8pm without adult supervision.

The resident also claims some young people have been seen sniffing glue and fighting, raising concerns about their safety.

In response to questions from fijivillage News, Assistant Commissioner of Police Operations Kasiano Vusonilawe has reminded parents and guardians to make their children's safety a priority.

Vusonilawe says parents must know where their children are, who they are spending time with, and ensure they return home safely.

He is also urging parents to make sure their children do not get involved with the wrong crowd.

item.title: We are all Fijians, Fiji is home to everyone – Qereqeretabua
item.description: We all are Fijians, w e may come from different backgrounds, but Fiji is home to all of us. Assistant Minister for Foreign Affairs Lenora Qereqeretabua stressed this in a social media post.
item.content:encoded:
We all are Fijians, w e may come from different backgrounds, but Fiji is home to all of us.

Assistant Minister for Foreign Affairs Lenora Qereqeretabua stressed this in a social media post.

Qereqeretabua is calling for greater understanding among Fiji's different communities, saying people should make an effort to learn about one another's cultures and languages.

She was born in Lautoka and grew up in Suva, Nadi and Sigatoka, where she developed an appreciation for different cultures.

She recalls growing up with Indo-Fijian friends, learning Hindi, taking part in cultural activities and spending time with Indo-Fijian families.

She says learning another community's language and traditions does not mean losing one's own cultural identity.

Qereqeretabua also remembers attending her Hindu landlord's cremation when she was eight years old and playing with his grandchildren.

She says these experiences did not mean losing touch with her iTaukei roots in Kadavu, Naitasiri and Matuku.

Qereqeretabua also shares that her grandson has Rotuman heritage and says she wants him to learn the language of his ancestors.

Reflecting on her move from the Western Division to Suva in 1987, she says she was surprised to find that people did not understand one another's languages as much as she had experienced in the Western and Northern divisions.

Qereqeretabua believes genuine respect comes from making an effort to understand other people's cultures and languages.

She is urging people to move away from division and recognise that Fiji is home to everyone.

item.title: PM assures public their views on Constitution Bill will be considered
item.description: Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka has assured members of the public that their submissions on the Constitution (Amendment) Bill 2026 will be considered by the Special Committee before the Bill proceeds to its third reading in Parliament next month. Speaking during the public consultation at the Nadi Civic Centre Hall, Rabuka, who chairs the Special Committee says the views and concerns raised will be
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka has assured members of the public that their submissions on the Constitution (Amendment) Bill 2026 will be considered by the Special Committee before the Bill proceeds to its third reading in Parliament next month.

Speaking during the public consultation at the Nadi Civic Centre Hall, Rabuka, who chairs the Special Committee says the views and concerns raised will be discussed during the Committee's deliberations later this month.

The consultation provided an opportunity for members of the public to ask questions, express their views and make submissions on the proposed constitutional amendments.

Rabuka thanked those who attended and contributed to the discussions, including those who made written submissions, while acknowledging the importance of public participation in the constitutional review process.

The next public consultation will be held tomorrow at the Ba Market Hall from 10am to 1pm.

item.title: No injuries reported after rental car catches fire near Nausori Airport
item.description: No injuries have been reported after a rental car caught fire near the Nausori Airport junction last night. The National Fire Authority confirms that firefighters from Nausori responded to the incident and extinguished the blaze.
item.content:encoded:
No injuries have been reported after a rental car caught fire near the Nausori Airport junction last night.

The National Fire Authority confirms that firefighters from Nausori responded to the incident and extinguished the blaze.

The NFA says the driver was present at the scene when firefighters arrived.

They sas an electrical fault is suspected to have caused the fire.

Questions have been sent to Police for further details on the incident.
